properties of the underlying mathematical functions, rather than based on the syntax used to denote
them.…

A measure is defined to be an outer measure that is countably additive on
measurable sets, with the additional assumption that the outer measure is the canonical
extension of the restricted measure.

The measure of a set `s`, denoted `μ s`, is an extended nonnegative real. The real-valued version
is written `μ.real s`.

A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `Set.ofPred` (also written `{x | p x}`) and membership of a set (`∈`) should be
used to convert between sets and predicates.

`Finset α` is the type of finite sets of elements of `α`. It is implemented
as a multiset (a list up to permutation) which has no duplicate elements.

`Multiset α` is the quotient of `List α` by list permutation. The result
is a type of finite sets with duplicates allowed.

Lean syntax trees.

the macro expander, and elaborated. They are also produced by the delaborator and presented to
users.

Linked lists: ordered lists, in which each element has a reference to the next element.

Most operations on linked lists take time proportional to the length of the list, because each

HurwitzZeta.evenKernel_functional_equation (a : UnitAddCircle) (x : ℝ) :

jacobiTheta₂_functional_equation (z τ : ℂ) :
  jacobiTheta₂ z τ =
    1 / (-Complex.I * τ) ^ (1 / 2) * Complex.exp (-↑Real.pi * Complex.I * z ^ 2 / τ) * jacobiTheta₂ (z / τ) (-1 / τ)

The functional equation for the Jacobi theta function: `jacobiTheta₂ z τ` is an explicit factor
times `jacobiTheta₂ (z / τ) (-1 / τ)`. This is the key lemma behind the proof of the functional
equation for L-series of even Dirichlet characters.

A filter `F` on a type `α` is a collection of sets of `α` which contains the whole `α`,
is upwards-closed, and is stable under intersection. We do not forbid this collection to be
all sets of `α`.

`Filter.Tendsto` is the generic "limit of a function" predicate.
`Tendsto f l₁ l₂` asserts that for every `l₂` neighborhood `a`,
the `f`-preimage of `a` is an `l₁` neighborhood.

A metric space is a type endowed with a `ℝ`-valued distance `dist` satisfying
`dist x y = 0 ↔ x = y`, commutativity `dist x y = dist y x`, and the triangle inequality
`dist x z ≤ dist x y + dist y z`.

See pseudometric spaces (`PseudoMetricSpace`) for the similar class with the `dist x y = 0 ↔ x = y`

over the boundary of a rectangle equals zero. More precisely, if `f` is complex differentiable on a
closed rectangle, then its integral over the boundary of the rectangle equals zero.

  [TopologicalSpace F] (f : 𝕜 → F) (x : 𝕜) : F

Derivative of `f` at the point `x`, if it exists.  Zero otherwise.

If the derivative exists (i.e., `∃ f', HasDerivAt f f' x`), then
`f x' = f x + (x' - x) • deriv f x + o(x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x`.

asserts that there is some `x` of type `α` such that `p x` holds.
To create an existential proof, use the `exists` tactic,
or the anonymous constructor notation `⟨x, h⟩`.

constructors for `Or`, called `Or.inl : a → a ∨ b` and `Or.inr : b → a ∨ b`,
and you can use `match` or `cases` to destruct an `Or` assumption into the
two cases.
